title: Autonomous Russian drone picked its own target, the chip slipped the export controls - TCR 08/25/26
description:

case prosecutors allege that a Southeast Asian intermediary bought roughly $2.5 billion in servers in 2024 and 2025 as part of a scheme that diverted servers to China, and the U.S.

This episode covers what a CSIS expert said would be the first documented case of a Russian self-targeting drone killing civilians with no human in the final targeting loop, the Jetson Orin diffusion problem, the Taiwan AI-server smuggling indictments, the post-quantum migration across Treasury, the Trusted Computing Group, and the Safeheron pilot, EvoMax building a compact gene editor at 97% editing efficiency, and Britain training battlefield-derived AI on protesters at home.

The through-line is capability outrunning the frameworks built to contain it. Investigators believe a Molniya drone identified a gas station on its own on July 6, running on a mass-market Nvidia module found inside four families of Russian weapons, while a Taiwanese court indicted nine people over 130 restricted B300 servers moved with forged documents. The defensive side moved just as fast: the U.S. Treasury and Bank of England co-chaired the G7 Cyber Expert Group, which brought financial authorities together to publish a quantum-readiness roadmap, a hardware body published quantum-safe benchmarks buyers can verify, and a fintech pilot will test NIST's ML-DSA-65 standard through wallet creation and on-chain transfers on the NEAR testnet, with the code headed for open source. An AI-guided method called EvoMax evolved a compact Fanzor2 editor, FanzMAX v3-hLa, that edited a human gene up to 97 percent of the time and beat the best prior compact editors more than 2.6-fold, with in-vivo cholesterol-gene editing in humanized mice. FERC filings in Wisconsin and Illinois are repricing data-center transmission costs back to the loads that create them, with Microsoft asking regulators to keep those costs off households. And Britain became the first foreign partner to Ukraine's Avengers AI Labs, piloting battlefield-trained sensing whose stated scope names protesters before anyone else.
